Trilingual Civic Glossary

Government & Legal Terms Explained

Confused by terms like affidavit, notary, self-attested, or gazette notification? Here are clear, Class-8 explanations in English, Hindi (हिंदी), and Gujarati (ગુજરાતી) so you never get misled by agents.

Affidavit

शपथ पत्र (Affidavit)•સોગંદનામું (Affidavit)
Class 8

A written statement sworn before an authorized notary or magistrate. It legally confirms that the facts stated by you are 100% true. Making a false affidavit is a criminal offense.

Who issues it:

Drafted on non-judicial stamp paper and signed before an Executive Magistrate or Notary Public.

Typical cost: ₹50 or ₹100 stamp paper + ₹50 notary attestation fee.Read details

Annexure

अनुलग्नक (Annexure)•જોડાણ (Annexure)
Class 8

A standardized affidavit or declaration form attached to a government application to certify specific circumstances (such as citizenship declaration, spouse details, or lost document explanation).

Who issues it:

Official format downloaded from the government portal and filled by the applicant.

Typical cost: Free download; printed on plain paper or stamp paper as specified.Read details

Challan / E-Challan

चालान (Challan)•ચલણ (Challan)
Class 8

An official computerized receipt or payment demand note used to deposit statutory fees or penalties directly into the government treasury.

Who issues it:

State treasury department, traffic police, or Parivahan portal.

Typical cost: Matches the exact statutory fee or penalty.Read details

Domicile Certificate

मूल निवास प्रमाण पत्र (Domicile)•રહેઠાણ પ્રમાણપત્ર (Domicile)
Class 8

An official certificate issued by the state revenue department certifying that a person has been residing permanently in that particular state for a specified duration (usually 10 to 15 years).

Who issues it:

Tehsildar, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), or Mamlatdar.

Typical cost: ₹20 – ₹50 statutory fee on state citizen portal.Read details

Gazette (Rajpatra)

राजपत्र (Gazette)•રાજપત્ર (Gazette)
Class 8

The official government publication where new statutes, statutory fee revisions, and legal name changes are published to make them legally recognized across India.

Who issues it:

Department of Publication, Government of India (Central Gazette) or State Government Printing Press.

Typical cost: ₹1,100 – ₹1,500 for legal name change notification.Read details

No Objection Certificate (NOC)

अनापत्ति प्रमाण पत्र (NOC)•વાંધા પ્રમાણપત્ર મુક્તિ (NOC)
Class 8

An official document issued by a government authority, employer, or financer stating that they have zero objection to a requested transaction or application.

Who issues it:

RTO (Form 28 for vehicle transfer), Police department, or financing bank.

Typical cost: ₹100 (Form 28 at RTO).Read details

Notary / Notarised

नोटरी (Notary)•નોટરી (Notary)
Class 8

A government-appointed legal officer (advocate) authorized to verify your identity, witness your signature, and place an official seal and stamp on legal declarations.

Who issues it:

Advocates appointed as Notaries by the Central or State Law Department.

Typical cost: ₹30 – ₹50 per signature/seal.Read details

Self-Attested

स्व-प्रमाणित (Self-Attested)•સ્વ-પ્રમાણિત (Self-Attested)
Class 8

Writing 'Self-Attested' on a photocopy, followed by your regular signature and the current date. It certifies that the photocopy is a true copy of your original document. No gazetted officer or seal is required.

Who issues it:

Done directly by you (the applicant).

Typical cost: Free (₹0).Read details

Tatkaal Scheme

तत्काल सेवा (Tatkal)•તત્કાલ યોજના (Tatkal)
Class 8

An official expedited fast-track government scheme that delivers passports or public services in 1 to 3 business days for an additional gazetted surcharge.

Who issues it:

Passport Seva Kendra (Ministry of External Affairs).

Typical cost: ₹2,000 additional statutory surcharge for passport.Read details
